rule_applied: SCHEMA.md F-2 pin: `inapprox` = NO poly-time f(n)-approximation for ANY polynomial f (unconditional unless P=NP). A problem with an n^eps-approx, a polylog gap, or conditional-only hardness is NOT `inapprox`.

entries.reason: A single vertex is already an n-approximation; Feige (SIDMA 2004) gives O(n(loglog n)^2/(log n)^3). An n^(1-eps) lower bound sits BELOW the achieved n-factor and cannot rule out polynomial factors.
entries.citation: Feige, Approximating maximum clique by removing subgraphs, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 18 (2004) [upper]; Hastad, Acta Math. 182 (1999) [lower]

entries.reason: MAX-IS is the textbook poly-APX-COMPLETE problem, which is incompatible with `inapprox`; trivial single-vertex n-approximation, improved to O(n(loglog n)^2/(log n)^3).
Using n colors is an n-approximation (chi >= 1); Halldorsson (IPL 1993) achieves O(n(loglog n)^2/(log n)^3). Zuckerman's n^(1-eps) is below the achieved polynomial factor.
entries.citation: Halldorsson, A still better performance guarantee for approximate graph coloring, IPL 45 (1993) [upper]; Zuckerman, Theory of Computing 3 (2007) [lower]
entries.additional_defect: OBJECT MISMATCH: problem_id is 3-COLORING but canonical_task states CHROMATIC NUMBER. Under the 3-colorable promise the best known algorithm uses ~O(n^0.19747) colors — an n^eps-approximation, which the F-2 pin names verbatim as disqualifying. The row needs an owner ruling on which object it is.

entries.reason: A 1-vertex mapping is an n-approximation; Halldorsson gives O(sqrt(n)) for maximum common induced subgraph. Kann (STACS 1992) shows it is only AS HARD AS MAX-IS, which is itself poly-APX-complete.

A uniformly random assignment satisfies half the equations in expectation (derandomizable by conditional expectations) = a 2-approximation. Hastad's (1/2+eps) bound proves that CONSTANT is tight — i.e. APX-hardness, not the absence of any polynomial factor.
entries.citation: Hastad, Some optimal inapproximability results, JACM 48 (2001) [tight constant]; random-assignment/derandomization [upper]

entries.reason: Micciancio proves NP-hardness only within SOME CONSTANT (sqrt2-eps) and only under RANDOMIZED reductions (NP not-subset RP, not P!=NP) — the pin rejects both constant-factor and conditional-only hardness. Poly-factor NP-hardness is barred anyway: O(sqrt n)-GapSVP is in coNP (Aharonov-Regev, JACM 2005), which would collapse PH. VOCABULARY GAP: best poly-time factor is 2^O(n loglog n/log n) — SUPERPOLYNOMIAL — so it cannot be demoted to poly-APX either. NO v1 rung is correct.
entries.resolution: owner ruling required — needs a v2 vocabulary rung (superpolynomial-but-not-inapprox) or an explicit `open` + note.

entries.reason: Dinur-Kindler-Raz-Safra prove hardness only within n^(c/loglog n) = 2^(log^(1-eps) n), which is n^o(1) — SUB-polynomial, precisely the 'almost-polynomial' case the pin excludes (the row's own task text says so). Same Aharonov-Regev/Goldreich-Goldwasser sqrt(n) barrier. Best poly-time factor 2^(n/2) (Babai) is superpolynomial, so poly-APX is also wrong.
entries.resolution: owner ruling required — same vocabulary gap as SVP.

entries.reason: VALUE STANDS but the WARRANT IS WRONG. Sahni-Gonzalez Thm 3.1 defines eps-approximate for a CONSTANT eps (Burkard-Cela's QAP survey quotes it as 'for an arbitrary eps>0') — APX-hardness only, matching the row's own 'no constant-factor' task text, which is below the pin.
entries.citation: REPLACE WITH: Queyranne (1986), who proves QAP is not approximable within ANY FINITE RATIO.

holds.reason: Sahni-Gonzalez's gadget sets w=1 on edges and a FREE PARAMETER k on non-edges, so k = n*alpha(n)+2 rules out every poly-time-computable alpha(n). Johnson & McGeoch state it as 'no heuristic can guarantee A(I)/OPT(I) <= 2^p(N) for any fixed polynomial p'.
holds.caveat: Survives on the universally accepted reading of the free gadget parameter (Vazirani Thm 3.6; Johnson & McGeoch Thm A). Sahni-Gonzalez's LITERAL Thm 3.1 is stated for constant eps — under a strictly literal citation standard TSP would also be CITE-INSUFFICIENT. Owner call.

systemic_note: Four independent v3 drafters made the identical F-2 mistake, and the v1 drafting process was not structurally different — which is why the sweep was ordered. 8 of 9 frozen `inapprox` cells were defective. The failure mode is treating an n^(1-eps) or 2^(log^(1-eps) n) LOWER bound as if it established the absence of ANY polynomial-factor UPPER bound. The two are independent; the pin requires the upper-bound side.
